final_answer:
>>> The Rosetta Stone is significant because it was the key to deciphering ancient Egyptian hieroglyphics, which had been a mystery for centuries.  
>>> It helped decode hieroglyphics because it contained the same text written in three scripts: Greek, Demotic, and hieroglyphs. Since Greek was already understood, scholars could use it as a reference to unlock the meaning of the other two scripts.  
>>> The breakthrough came when Jean-François Champollion, a French scholar, realized that hieroglyphs were not purely symbolic but also phonetic, combining logographic and alphabetic elements. This insight allowed him to translate hieroglyphs into modern languages.  
>>> By comparing the Greek text with the hieroglyphs, Champollion identified the names of Egyptian pharaohs and other words, gradually piecing together the structure of the language.  
>>> This discovery revolutionized the study of ancient Egypt, enabling scholars to read historical texts, religious inscriptions, and administrative records, thereby unlocking a vast repository of knowledge about Egyptian civilization.
